title: Hetmyer Steels Nerves as West Indies Chase Down 269 in Thriller
excerpt: Shimron Hetmyer's unbeaten 69 guided the hosts home after a dramatic late collapse in the fifth ODI against New Zealand at Kensington Oval.
body:
Shimron Hetmyer held his nerve under mounting pressure to steer West Indies to a thrilling two-wicket victory over New Zealand in the fifth and final ODI at Kensington Oval, Bridgetown, ensuring the hosts finished the series with a consolation win despite losing the rubber 3-2.

Chasing 269, West Indies were cruising at 218/4 before a dramatic late collapse saw them slump to 248/8 in the space of four overs. Hetmyer, unbeaten on 69 off 64 balls, refused to buckle and shepherded the tail home with 15 balls to spare.

Hetmyer and Rutherford Revive the Chase

West Indies made an explosive start to their innings. Openers Ackeem Auguste (34) and Justin Greaves (22) raced to 57 in just 5.5 overs before Nathan Smith and Jacob Duffy struck in quick succession. Keacy Carty struggled to a laboured 20 off 54 balls with no boundaries as the required rate climbed, and when he and captain Shai Hope (39) departed in the space of two overs, West Indies found themselves at 123/4 and in danger of capitulation.

Hetmyer and Sherfane Rutherford transformed the contest with a fifth-wicket partnership of 95 off 90 balls. Rutherford, the more aggressive of the pair, cracked 61 off 58 deliveries before being stumped by Tom Latham off Michael Bracewell in the 41st over.

A Late Wobble

Rutherford's dismissal at 218/5 opened the floodgates. Jayden Lennox, who finished with 3-35, dismissed Gudakesh Motie in the 44th over to claim his third wicket of the match and push his series tally to 14 — the highest by any bowler in the series. In the very next over, Jacob Duffy produced a devastating spell, bowling Matthew Forde and then having Alzarri Joseph caught for a first-ball duck. West Indies had slumped to 248/8 with 21 runs still required.

“Hetmyer watched on from the other end as West Indies slipped to a tricky situation at 248/8. But he soldiered on and saw the chase through.”

— Cricbuzz match report

Hetmyer, who had played second fiddle to Rutherford during their partnership, took charge of the chase. With Jayden Seales blocking at the other end, the Guyanese left-hander picked off singles and found the occasional boundary to bring the target within reach. West Indies crossed the line with 15 balls to spare, reaching 269/8 in 47.3 overs.

New Zealand's Three Fifties in Vain

Earlier, New Zealand posted the highest total of the series — 268/9 in 50 overs — thanks to half-centuries from three batters. Will Young (56) and Nick Kelly (64) added 86 for the second wicket after Henry Nicholls fell early to Matthew Forde. Captain Tom Latham anchored the second half of the innings with a fluent 69 off 71 balls, finding useful support from Mitchell Santner and Duffy toward the end.

The Black Caps were unable to produce the late acceleration needed to push beyond 270, losing wickets at regular intervals during the death overs. Alzarri Joseph and Vitel Lawes took two wickets each for West Indies, with Forde, Seales and Motie picking up one apiece.

Series Verdict

New Zealand take the series 3-2, but West Indies will draw encouragement from this final-day fightback and the individual performances of Hetmyer and Rutherford. The Caribbean side now turns its attention to a home Test series against Pakistan, beginning on July 25 at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba, Trinidad.
